o1.biggest_strength: The reply-rate forecast is honest. It is anchored at 6.8% to 7.9% from the pilot and refuses to multiply two effects the pilot never tested together. It also spots that the 1,300 pilot Controllers who already got the old sequence need a rest period.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some lines are clunky. Step 4's 'the 9 to 4 day close I shared is the reason I wrote' reads awkwardly. Step 3's subject assumes they have an audit coming.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the step 4 wording and make the step 3 subject neutral. Show the pilot-wide baseline next to the projection so I can see the lift at a glance.

o2.biggest_strength: The presentation is very clear. The 'who, when, how' summary and the leave-out table are easy to follow. The comparison against the pilot-wide baseline (3.1%, 1.4%, 1.2%) is calculated correctly, and step 3 usefully brings engineering into the conversation.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 8% forecast with a 10% ceiling rests on a made-up 1.25 multiplier, and the 7% floor sits above what this segment actually did (6.8%). It also never says to hold back the pilot Controllers who were already contacted.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Ground the forecast in the pilot numbers alone and drop the invented multiplier. Exclude contacts from the earlier sequence. Replace the stock subject 'Closing the loop'.

reason: Both nail the segment, the trigger and the no-link rule. Output 1 gives me a forecast I can defend and catches the re-contact problem. Output 2 reads more cleanly but pads the expected reply rate with an assumed multiplier.
